bug_report_content:
id: 772
status: Fixed
summary: JSCompiler does not recursively resolve typedefs
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 6
Comment 0 (2012-07-06): goog.provide('a.b.c'); goog.scope(function() { var b = a.b; var c = b.c; /** @typedef {string} */ c.MyType; /** @param {c.MyType} x The variable. */ c.myFunc = function(x) {}; }); results in a compiler error. given that JSCompiler *does* recursively resolve other names, this appears to be a bug rather than an intended limitation.
Comment 1 (2012-07-06): I'm fairly certain that typedefs have to be in the global scope. Although I'm not sure that has been documented anywhere or is the intent. If you remove the goog.scope wrapper, your code compiles correctly.
Comment 2 (2012-07-06): no, typedefs don't have to be in the global scope. goog.scope must enclose everything in the file except goog.provide/goog.require
Comment 3 (2012-07-06): Scope affects it in some way. Here's test code: var foo = {}; /** @typedef {string} */ foo.bar; /** @typedef {string} */ var foo2; var foo3 = {}; (function() { /** @typedef {string} */ foo3.bar; /** @typedef {string} */ var foo4; var foo5 = {}; /** @typedef {string} */ foo5.bar; /** @param {foo.bar} x The variable. */ var myFunc = function(x) {}; // No errors /** @param {foo2} x The variable. */ var myFunc2 = function(x) {}; // No errors /** @param {foo3.bar} x The variable. */ var myFunc3 = function(x) {}; // Unknown type error /** @param {foo4} x The variable. */ var myFunc4 = function(x) {}; // Unknown type error /** @param {foo5.bar} x The variable. */ var myFunc5 = function(x) {}; // Unknown type error })();
Comment 4 (2012-07-07): for the record, the error message is: JSC_TYPE_PARSE_ERROR: Bad type annotation. Unknown type c.MyType at line 10 character 12 /** @param {c.MyType} x The variable. */
Comment 5 (2012-07-09): This issue was closed by revision r2077.
